input.question: How come the F-35 program cost way more to develop than the F-22 despite being generally less technologically advanced?
input.ground_truth: F-35 is pretty much 3 different planes, that look similar. * Navy version has different wings and modifications to frame to support carrier landing. * Marine version has VSTOL. * Air Force version has better performance.

Explain the following question in a simple way as if you are explaining to a 5-year-old.

Question: How come the F-35 program cost way more to develop than the F-22 despite being generally less technologically advanced?

Answer:

response.prediction:
Okay, let’s imagine you and your friend both want to build a super cool toy car. You want yours to do lots of different tricks, like flying really far, hiding from others, and changing its shape a little. Your friend just wants a fast, strong car that’s really good at one thing.

Now, you decide your toy car needs to be able to play with kids in many different playgrounds all over the world. So you have to make sure it works with every kind of slide, swing, and sandbox everywhere. You also want everyone to help pay for it, so lots of people have ideas about what it should do. Every time someone suggests a new idea, you have to change your plan a little.

Your friend’s car was only for one special playground, and not as many people were giving ideas about what it should do. So, your toy car takes much longer to build, and you spend a lot more money trying to make everyone happy and fit it for every playground.

That’s kind of like what happened with the F-35 and the F-22. The F-35 was supposed to be used by lots of countries and do many different jobs, so it got more changes and had to fit more rules. The F-22 was just for one country and had a simpler job, so it was easier and cheaper to make—even though some parts of it were more advanced. But because the F-35 had to do so many things and please so many people, it ended up costing way more money to make.
